title: Two-day Power Ministers’ Conference begins in New Delhi
subtitle:
Rs 200 lakh Crore Investment Opportunity in the Power Sector in Next Two Decades
Demands Teamwork of all Stakeholders: Shri Manohar Lal
body_text: The two-day Power Ministers’ Conference commenced in New Delhi today. The conference (November 27-28, 2026) brings together Power Ministers, senior officials and electricity regulators from 28 States and 8 Union Territories and is chaired by Shri Manohar Lal, Union Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs. The last such conference at the national level was held in 2024. The Conference provides a platform for Centre–State deliberations on key policy priorities and implementation challenges in India’s power sector, with discussions focusing on strengthening energy security, improving power infrastructure and accelerating sectoral reforms. While welcoming the participating State Power Ministers and other dignitaries, Shri Manohar Lal emphasised the need for the Centre and States to work together to develop the power sector. He said that India has made significant progress in expanding generation capacity, integrating renewable energy and strengthening the national grid. The next phase of our journey requires us to move towards a more integrated approach to power sector planning, where generation, storage, transmission and distribution are planned as interconnected elements of a single system. He stressed the necessity for States to implement Smart Meters, which offer significant benefits to consumers. The Minister also stated that, through collaboration with States and initiatives from the Ministry of Power, DISCOMS have achieved profitability after a prolonged period. The Minister noted that the country’s power sector presents investment opportunity of Rs 200 lakh crores over the next two decades, and all stakeholders have to work together to make this possible. We have to work together with the private sector to ensure that we accomplish this, he said. Shri Manohar Lal complimented the States and DISCOMs, as the DISCOMs as a whole turned a positive PAT during FY 2024-25. He said that we need to ensure that financial position of our DISCOMs is strengthened and necessary changes in policy, operations and regulation should facilitate the continuation of this turnaround. While listing the main agenda of the Conference, he informed that Conference will comprise interactions and in-depth discussions among the Ministry of Power, States and other stakeholders on key issues such as implementation of Resource Adequacy (RA) plans, including accelerated energy storage deployment; inter-state and intra-state transmission issues; financial viability of Distribution Companies (DISCOMs); implementation of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with emphasis on smart metering, feeder separation and household electrification; and issues related to nuclear sites. Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power in his address asked the participating States and UTs to share their experiences during the Conference, including difficulties in implementation, regulatory issues and areas where further support or intervention from the Central Government may be required. Our collective focus should be on moving from policy formulation to effective execution, from infrastructure creation to measurable outcomes, and from individual interventions to an integrated and sustainable power sector, the Minister said. While addressing the participants, Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power noted that the core guidance received from the Prime Minister is to move beyond energy security toward true energy independence in service of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. The past year has been one of record growth, he said, and noted that India’s installed capacity is now about 563 GW, and more than 55% of it is non-fossil. In the last 12 months around 60 GW of capacity was added, 87% of it from non-fossil sources, he said. A key highlight on November 28 will be a joint session with the Forum of Regulators and State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs), bringing together State Power Ministers, SERC Chairpersons, State Secretaries for Power/Energy and Ministry officials to deliberate on issues concerning the power sector. Senior officials from the Ministry of Power and representatives from participating States and Union Territories are also attending the Conference. *** NR/AP/MD
